title: Punch Bench
summary: Simulate a curve-driven punch and watch two arrows: how far the bat has moved from its start, and how fast it is going — which flips around the moment the strike becomes a return.
why: A punch built on SetRelativeLocation animates perfectly and moves nothing. Seeing the velocity arrow appear, reverse and vanish while the offset arrow stays put is what separates two things that look identical on screen: where a body is, and how fast it is going.

title: Normalize Bench
summary: Drag a vector's tip around a grid and watch its normalized copy stay pinned to the unit circle while the raw x, y and length keep changing.
why: Normalizing looks like it throws information away. Seeing the ratio between x and y hold perfectly steady while the length varies is what makes it land that direction and distance are two separate facts stored in the same three numbers.

title: Snake Vector Bench
summary: Write each step of the segment-follow math as an expression, watch it drawn on a grid, then have it checked at eight random positions.
why: The follow math fails in a way that looks correct: an answer built from hardcoded offsets lines up perfectly for one arrangement of the segments and is wrong for every other. Re-checking at random positions is the only thing that catches it.
